propositions: Packaged prose guides cite criterion ids inline without any coupling to the criteria registry, allowing criterion rubrics to be rewritten while guide paraphrases silently become inaccurate.
No systematic mechanism exists to detect when a criterion's authoritative registry text changes in a way that contradicts claims made about it in packaged prose guides.
A gate must pin digests of cited criteria and fail visibly when a criterion's text changes, forcing re-verification and re-pinning of the guide's claims.
The pin manifest is derived, not hand-authored, and lives alongside the guides it protects so it ships and is diffable in review.

Citation extraction uses vocabulary-only matching against the registry's closed criterion-id set at word boundaries, independent of guide markup or structure, so ordinary prose edits do not break the gate.
